summary: Refined the last open repair-path limit from an untested path to a reasoned negative. I acquired the voter-side vote-admission rule as a source and recorded the fact it establishes: a candidate is granted votes only if its log is at least as up to date as the voter's, so once the conflicting entries are committed at the highest index of every log in the same term, no later leader can write a different entry at that index — it can only append beyond it, where the same-term duplicate skip leaves the difference untouched. That means the divergence left by this defect can only be removed by replacing a node's state (a snapshot install for a node that falls behind a compacted leader, or a leader-side restore that converges the cluster), which are exactly the two mechanisms the earlier receipts exercised; the previously listed "term truncation not exercised" limitation becomes that argument, with the residual caveat that a variant of the defect leaving a shorter log on a node that could still win votes would change it. Both the repair-path interpretation (no defect judgment of its own) and the child question's account were rewritten around that, with joint histories extended across the receipt chain. Remaining work: none of the registered questions has an open necessary gap; the standing limits are the harness-arranged lag for the per-node repair, the self-produced snapshot for the restore, single samples per mode, in-memory stores with scaled timeouts, and the injected wrapper snapshot store used for the constructor-stall reachability.
